Chorzow Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Chorzów, Poland

Demolished. Chorzów formed through the merger of the historic village Chareu (established 1257) and the industrial settlement Königshütte (founded 1799, town rights 1868); the combined agglomeration joined newly independent Poland after WWI. Jews are recorded from 1829, with a prayer house from around 1850 and a grand 1875 brick synagogue; the community gained independence from Bytom's kehilla in 1865, reaching 4,705 residents before WWII. In 1940, Germans deported local Jews via Olkusz and Jaworzno to Auschwitz-Birkenau. This cemetery, established in 1862, was expanded and walled in the early 20th century. Burials continued until 1954, with the state formally closing the cemetery in 1958 and later ordering its full liquidation in 1973 - exhumed remains were transferred to Bytom's Jewish cemetery, tombstones removed, and the land converted into a public park (marked with a 2006 commemorative monument).
